title: Today We Rule in Our Valley
intro: At the end of Shawqi’s “The Sphinx”, the statue’s breast opens and a young man and woman step out to sing. After a poet’s conversation with an ancient monument, the valley’s children speak in the first person about the country they want to build. The watching temple and pyramid give way to a call for work and a last line sung twice, exactly as printed. Osama Al-Waaedh recites the entire closing song.

translation: Today we rule in our valley
and bring back the glories of our past.
1.sharh: The boy and girl speak as “we”, taking in everyone in the valley. Their first word is “today”, and the past enters as something their generation can bring back.

translation: And through our hands glory is raised
by a homeland we would ransom, and which ransoms us.
2.sharh: Only in the second half do we hear the subject that raises glory through their hands. People and country then exchange the roles of rescuer and rescued.

translation: A homeland we uphold with justice
and build under God’s eye.
3.sharh: The singers pick up “a homeland” from the previous line. Upholding it has a moral condition, and building it takes place under a watchful eye.

translation: We make it fair and give it adornment
through our noble deeds and our efforts.
4.sharh: The ornaments promised in the first half turn out to be actions. A deed worth remembering and the effort of doing it are both ways of making the country beautiful.

translation: The secret of history and its very substance,
the throne of time and its pulpit,
5.sharh: The sequence gives history a secret and a substance, then gives time two public seats. One belongs to a ruler, the other to someone addressing an assembly.

translation: the gardens of eternity and its river Kawthar,
our forebears suffice us for fragrant herbs.
6.sharh: Gardens and the river of Paradise lend their colours to the valley. For the fragrance of the garden, the singers have the memory of their ancestors.

translation: We take the sun for its crown
and its morning light for a dazzling throne,
7.sharh: The sun becomes regalia that can be set on the country’s head. Its light furnishes the throne as well, so the whole royal figure shines.

translation: and the sky of high honour for its towers.
So it was with our forebears.
8.sharh: The towers complete a palace built out of light and honour. The ancestors now give the singers a precedent for imagining Egypt on this scale.

translation: Your age sees you, and so do the nations.
Karnak looks on, and the Pyramid.
9.sharh: The singers turn to address their listeners. Living nations watch from the present, while the temple and the pyramid acquire eyes with which the past can watch.

translation: Children of these lands, have you no ambitions
to build us up as the ancients built?
10.sharh: The monuments suggest a building project for the living. What ambition can build now is the people themselves.

translation: Always strive, strive and strive,
for deep-rooted glory and the heights.
11.sharh: The repeated noun for striving works like a command that can be sung in time. The object of effort has both deep roots and a height still to be reached.

translation: And let us make Egypt our whole world.
And let us make Egypt our whole world.
12.sharh: The two halves are identical on the printed page. The singers leave their audience with a complete sentence it can immediately sing back.

1.1.2.head: سادَ
1.1.2.meaning: To exercise sovereignty, here over one’s own country.

1.1.3.head: الوادي
1.1.3.meaning: The valley of the Nile, the Egypt named in the last line.

2.1.1.head: أَشادَ
2.1.1.meaning: Raises or builds high. Its subject, “a homeland”, comes in the next half.

2.2.2.head: فَدى
2.2.2.meaning: To ransom, to surrender something precious so that another may be safe.

4.2.1.head: مَأثُرَة
4.2.1.meaning: A noble deed that people remember and recount.

5.2.1.head: سَرير
5.2.1.meaning: A throne, the seat of sovereignty.

6.1.3.head: الكَوثَر
6.1.3.meaning: Kawthar, the river of Paradise, evoked through the image of water in Egypt.

6.2.3.head: رَيحان
6.2.3.meaning: Fragrant plants. The forebears supply the perfume of the imagined gardens.

7.2.1.head: الضُّحى
7.2.1.meaning: Morning at its brightness, when the light has spread.

9.2.1.head: الكَرنَك
9.2.1.meaning: Karnak, the ancient temple complex at Luxor, here a watching presence.

9.2.3.head: الهَرَم
9.2.3.meaning: The Pyramid, a monument of Egypt’s ancient kings standing witness to a new generation.

10.1.1-2.head: بَنو الأَوطان
10.1.1-2.meaning: “Children of the lands”: a direct address introduced by a short vocative particle.

11.2.1.head: أَثيل
11.2.1.meaning: Deep-rooted or of long standing, here describing glory.

11.2.3.head: العُليا
11.2.3.meaning: The highest station one can aspire to.
